name: gpt-oss-120b
purpose: OpenAI: production, general-purpose, high-reasoning use cases that fit a single 80 GB GPU; also agentic tasks with built-in tools.

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: LICENSE file in the repo read (11,357 bytes): standard Apache License 2.0, identical to the apache.org text apart from a trailing newline. The card adds no extra usage policy.

architecture.kind: MoE, MXFP4-quantized experts, harmony response format
architecture.drafter: EAGLE3 draft GGUF exists in ggml-org repo (0.85 GB Q8_0)
architecture.why_this_design: Not stated on the card beyond the target: 'production, general purpose, high reasoning use cases that fit into a single 80GB GPU' (117B parameters, 5.1B active).

pc-12gb.notes: 63 GB file; RAM would have to carry it.

pc-16gb.notes: Needs more than 64 GB RAM headroom; only 5.1 B active.

mac-64gb+.notes: 64 GB Mac working set 51-53 GB (docs/hardware); 96 GB+ fits.

engine_support.notes: A 2025-09 write-up found llama.cpp ran gpt-oss smoothly (20b tested).

benchmarks.name: INCLUDE (German, PeerBench DACH)
benchmarks.harness: PeerBench DACH German Language LLM Index

strengths: Three reasoning levels set in the system prompt
Native browsing, Python and function-calling tools; Apache-2.0
weaknesses: Hallucinates heavily on SimpleQA-style facts (a Substack post claims about 8 in 10 wrong; not checked against OpenAI's card)
Languages not stated on the card; mostly English-centric (unverified)
Over a year old: older than most of this set
soft.behavior: Must be used with the harmony format. Reasoning: low, medium or high in the system prompt.
best_for: Math and reasoning where a large knowledge base is not needed

user_reports.summary: Oumi evaluation: truthful but refuses too often.
Substack: gpt-oss-120b hallucinated on about 8 in 10 SimpleQA questions (20b: 9 in 10).

soft.maturity: OpenAI's first open weights since GPT-2; no newer open release found (research/49).

tona_fit.reason: Large (63 GB) and older; only 5.1B active so it suits RAM-rich machines, but the only independent German score (INCLUDE DE 66.2) trails the 2026 models (Qwen3.8-27B 87.9, Muse Glimmer 86.0) and its vendor knowledge numbers are lower. Missing Tona module is only a blocker.

sources.note: PeerBench DACH JSON export, read directly

open_questions: Layer and expert counts, context and languages are not on the card
OpenAI model-card SimpleQA figure not checked
